hints: Look carefully at how skeletal formulas work, every bend and end of a line is a carbon, even when C is not written.
Start by counting carbons and oxygens, they are all shown, there are 6 carbons and 7 oxygens in total.
Now add the hidden hydrogens to give each carbon four bonds, remember CH2 groups have two H each and OH and CO2H groups each add one H.
walkthrough:
**Count the carbon skeleton**

Every line end, bend and carbonyl C counts as one carbon. Let's trace them through.

$$\text{HO-C(=O)-CH}_2\text{-C-CH}_2\text{-C(=O)-OH plus one C in central CO}_2\text{H} = 6 \text{ C}$$

**Count the oxygens shown**

Oxygens are always drawn out, so just count the Os. There are three $\text{COOH}$ groups and one $\text{OH}$ group.

$$(3 \times 2) + 1 = 7 \text{ O}$$

**Add the hidden hydrogens**

In skeletal formulas, H on carbon is hidden. Give each carbon 4 bonds. The two $\text{CH}_2$ groups give $2 + 2 = 4$ H.

$$\text{3 } \times \text{ CO}_2\text{H H} + 1 \times \text{ OH H} + 4 \times \text{ CH}_2 \text{ H} = 3 + 1 + 4 = 8 \text{ H}$$

**Write the molecular formula**

Put C, then H, then O together. That gives $\text{C}_6\text{H}_8\text{O}_7$, which matches one of the options.

options.A: Correct. 6 carbons from the chain plus carbonyl carbons, 7 oxygens from three carboxylic acid groups plus one alcohol, and 8 hydrogens (4 on the two CH2 groups, 3 on the CO2H groups, 1 on the OH). This gives C6H8O7.
options.B: Incorrect. C6H4O7 has far too few hydrogens. This comes from forgetting the hidden H atoms on the two CH2 groups, each CH2 contributes two H atoms that are not drawn in skeletal formula.
options.C: Incorrect. C8H8O7 has too many carbons. This comes from miscounting line bends as extra carbons, or counting each C=O double bond as two carbons. Each carbonyl is only one carbon.
options.D: Incorrect. C10H8O7 has far too many carbons. This comes from counting every line segment as a separate carbon instead of counting vertices, a common error when first reading skeletal formulas.
